title: pseudognaphalium canescens subsp. thermale
intro: Pseudognaphalium canescens subsp. thermale, commonly known as Thermopytan or Hot Springs Gumweed, is a subspecies of flowering plant in the daisy family that is native to the southwestern United States. It has been used in traditional medicine for its various health benefits, which include anti-inflammatory and antimicrobial properties that aid in wound healing and reduce fever. The therapeutic actions of Thermopytan are attributed to its ability to exhibit antioxidant and anti-inflammatory activities, which contribute to its potential in treating various health conditions. The bioactive constituents of this plant include sesquiterpene lactones and phenolic compounds, which are responsible for its medicinal properties.
